core_findings: Core IBX economics are carrier-neutral retail colocation plus power and interconnection, complemented by managed infrastructure.
xScale adds hyperscale capacity mainly through equity-method joint ventures; atNorth adds Nordic high-density exposure through a partner-owned structure.
FY2025 revenue was 94.8139% recurring; colocation was about 70.25% and interconnection 17.96% of revenue.
Customer concentration is low, but the model is physically capital intensive and constrained by power, utility timing and site development.
business_model.rationale: The economic perimeter is well established and separates consolidated IBX operations from unconsolidated/JV economics.

core_findings: Recurring revenue, diversified customers, rising cabinet utilization and a large installed ecosystem support high operating visibility.
FY2025 adjusted EBITDA margin was 49.1483%, but that metric excludes SBC and other economic costs and is not a cash-return measure.
H1 2026 revenue growth was strong, yet part of the Americas increase included non-recurring services to joint ventures; headline growth should not be treated as purely organic recurring economics.
Physical infrastructure intensity, financing needs and power scarcity materially qualify the otherwise strong operating characteristics.
economic_quality.rationale: Operating quality is strong, but economic quality is not inferred from margins or recurrence alone.

canonical_verdict_fields.PRIMARY_MOAT: Dense interconnection ecosystem plus embedded colocation switching friction across strategically located carrier-neutral facilities.

core_findings: More than 10,500 customers, 2,000 network providers and 500,000 interconnections create density and coordination value.
Independent AWS and Google evidence confirms Equinix as a direct/private cloud interconnection location in multiple metros.
The mechanism is not exclusive: Google and competitor evidence show credible alternatives and multi-provider choice.
High recurrence and repeat bookings support embedded behavior, but contract termination flexibility means recurrence is not equivalent to hard contractual lock-in.
The absence of quantified customer migration economics prevents STRONGLY_SUPPORTED status.
unresolved_points: Standalone interconnection margin/incremental-return attribution remains unavailable.
Direct quantified migration/switching-cost evidence remains limited.
moat.rationale: Evidence converges on a real but non-exclusive ecosystem/embeddedness advantage; durability is bounded by strong alternative providers and incomplete switching evidence.

core_findings: The existing development program spans 52 major projects across 35 metros with more than 55,000 planned retail cabinets and more than 100 MW of xScale capacity through 2028.
Independent industry evidence shows tight vacancy and strong high-density/AI demand, supporting a meaningful demand runway.
The ~1 GW land-bank figure is not treated as energized capacity.
Power availability, grid lead times, permitting and capital availability are binding conversion constraints.
Inference Exchange is optionality only at the cutoff because commercial availability is announced for Q1 2027 with no realized adoption/economics.
runway.rationale: Demand and project evidence support a large extended runway, but supply conversion is constrained enough to prevent STRONGLY_SUPPORTED status.

core_findings: The all-in 2025 ROIC reconstruction is positive but modest at about 5.28%; the ex-goodwill diagnostic is about 6.47%.
A one-year incremental-return diagnostic is stronger, but it cannot be promoted to canonical ROIIC because construction, acquisitions/JVs and investment lag break attribution.
The xScale structure can improve balance-sheet sharing but obscures complete capital and return attribution across equity investments, loans, VIE exposure and related-party income.
Current evidence does not establish strong marginal returns on the full growth-capital program.
unresolved_points: Project/cohort returns for xScale and atNorth remain unproven.
return_quality.rationale: Positive operating economics do not translate into elite all-in capital productivity on the available evidence.

core_findings: Operating cash generation is strong, but total cash PP&E investment has exceeded CFO in 2025 and H1 2026.
AFFO is transparent and useful as a REIT operating measure, but it adds back SBC and relies on an issuer-defined recurring-capex measure that cannot be assumed to equal economic maintenance.
SBC is economically material and must remain a real compensation cost; capitalized SBC adds to the construction asset base.
No evidence of accounting failure is identified, but maintenance-capex ambiguity is material enough to keep forensic reliability at WATCH.
unresolved_points: Economic Owner Earnings cannot be responsibly bounded from cutoff evidence.
fcf_forensic.rationale: Cash reporting is traceable, yet the key economic bridge from AFFO to maintenance-adjusted owner cash remains uncertain.

core_findings: Capital allocation is growth-heavy: substantial organic development, JV equity/loans, real-estate acquisitions and the atNorth transaction are being funded alongside a large dividend.
Common shares outstanding increased from about 94.63 million at YE2023 to 98.226 million at YE2025, while ATM equity issuance and debt markets have been used to finance growth.
The partnership/JV model shares capital requirements, but full project/cohort returns are not disclosed.
atNorth expands high-density Nordic capacity, but realized utilization, return and exact recourse/accounting economics remain unproven at the cutoff.
capital_allocation.rationale: The record is mixed: strategic reinvestment capacity is substantial, but demonstrated incremental capital productivity is insufficient for a strong stewardship judgment.

core_findings: CEO Adaire Fox-Martin's incentive design includes revenue, AFFO per share and relative TSR, which introduces per-share and shareholder-return alignment.
Revenue remains a major annual-incentive driver and AFFO excludes several economic costs, so the plan does not directly impose a marginal-return or ROIC hurdle.
Current-leadership long-horizon capital-allocation attribution is limited in the cutoff evidence.
unresolved_points: Longitudinal outcome attribution under the current leadership remains limited.
management_governance.rationale: Alignment is meaningful but incomplete; governance evidence is adequate for a moderate-positive judgment, not an exceptional stewardship claim.

core_findings: Digital Realty, CoreSite, NTT, QTS and CyrusOne demonstrate that data-center and interconnection competition is deep and well capitalized.
Industry vacancy and demand evidence supports sector growth, but the Cyxtera case shows that strong demand can coexist with financial failure.
Sector outage data keeps power and connectivity failure as real base-rate risks rather than issuer-specific hypotheticals.
outside_view.rationale: The outside view validates demand but rejects any inference that demand alone guarantees superior returns or resilience.

risks.risk: Large debt and contractual commitments create refinancing/funding sensitivity.
Power availability, utility timing and high-density conversion can delay or strand capacity.
Alternative colocation/interconnection providers can constrain pricing and ecosystem exclusivity.
JV/VIE and atNorth structures can obscure full capital-at-risk and realized return attribution.
Power, sustainability, permitting and grid constraints can raise costs or limit expansion.
Capacity absorption and customer deployment cycles can soften even with long-run digital demand.

resilience_findings: More than 90% recurring revenue, low customer concentration, broad geography and substantial liquidity support resilience.
Debt, commitments and capital-market dependence prevent a high-resilience conclusion despite strong demand visibility.
risk_resilience.rationale: Business resilience is good, but financial and infrastructure-execution vulnerabilities are material.

dimension_scoring_inputs.rationale: Real ecosystem and embeddedness advantage, but not exclusive and switching-cost evidence is incomplete.
Large multi-year demand and project runway, materially constrained by power and deliverability.
Positive but modest all-in ROIC with canonical ROIIC not interpretable.
Strong CFO/AFFO visibility, offset by heavy capex, SBC and unbounded maintenance economics.
Mixed record: aggressive reinvestment and external financing without sufficiently demonstrated marginal returns.
Meaningful per-share/TSR alignment, but no direct ROIC hurdle and limited long-horizon attribution.
Diversified recurring architecture and liquidity, offset by leverage, commitments and power/execution risk.
